chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-A'ala who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever sells a palm tree that has been pollinated, the fruit belongs to the seller, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged with that.'

key_terms.لَقِحَ: pollinated (referring to the fruit set on the tree)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the fruit of a palm tree sold after pollination?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) grounds this commercial ruling in the precedent of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), highlighting the continuity of prophetic jurisprudence in trade contracts. This narration clarifies the default ownership of produce in 'sale of fruit' (Bay' al-Thamar) transactions, emphasizing that the fruit remains with the seller unless explicitly transferred, a principle crucial for avoiding ambiguity (Gharar) in Islamic commercial law.
